title: Quantum Cryptomania with Classical Communication without One-Way Functions
abstract: In classical cryptography, one-way functions are necessary for most of cryptography. In the quantum world, however, Kretschmer at {TQC'21} and subsequent works have demonstrated that quantum versions of various primitives in minicrypt, such as signatures and private-key encryption, do not require quantum-computable one-way functions (\textsf{qOWF}s). However, the question of the necessity of \textsf{qOWF}s for primitives in Cryptomania like public-key encryption with classical public keys and ciphertexts (\textsf{qPKE}) has remained open.   We provide a comprehensive picture of the relationship between \textsf{qPKE} and \textsf{qOWF}. First, our main result is a black-box separation between \textsf{qOWF}s and \textsf{qPKE}. In particular, we show that relative to a unitary, real, and self-inverse oracle, there exists a \textsf{qPKE} scheme (with classical keys and ciphertexts), but \textsf{qOWF}s do not exist. Further, our oracles admit a point-function obfuscation construction, thus ruling out black-box construction of \textsf{qOWF} from point function obfuscations.   On the positive side, we construct \textsf{qPKE} from quantum indistinguishability obfuscation for quantum circuits with classical obfuscated descriptions and efficiently verifiable one-way puzzles, which is known to be a potentially weaker assumption than \textsf{qOWF}s, due to an existing black-box separation. Our construction is the quantum analog of the classical construction of \textsf{PKE} from one-way functions and indistinguishability obfuscation in the quantum computation with classical communication (QCCC) setting.
summary: This paper deeply analyzes the necessary computational assumptions for quantum public-key encryption (qPKE) in a classical communication setting. It proves a black-box separation demonstrating that qPKE can exist even when quantum one-way functions (qOWFs) do not. Furthermore, it provides a constructive link, showing qPKE can be built from quantum indistinguishability obfuscation, thus refining our understanding of quantum cryptographic foundations.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental relationship between quantum-computable one-way functions (qOWFs) and quantum public-key encryption (qPKE) when communication and keys are restricted to classical channels.
main_result: A black-box separation is established showing that a qPKE scheme can exist without the existence of qOWFs, and conversely, qPKE can be constructed from weaker assumptions like quantum indistinguishability obfuscation.
method: The authors employ black-box separation techniques using specific oracles, alongside constructive proofs that build qPKE from other quantum primitives.
model_or_system: The theoretical model is the Quantum Computation with Classical Communication (QCCC) setting, focusing on cryptographic primitives like qPKE and qOWFs.
key_observables: IND-CPA security, existence/non-existence of qOWFs (qOWF1, qOWF2, qOWF3), and the relationship between qPKE and these functions.
important_parameters: The separation relies on the existence of a specific unitary, real, and self-inverse oracle.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the black-box model for cryptographic primitives, and the separation results are conditional on the existence of specific oracles.
figures_summary: Figure 1 summarizes the complex implications, equivalences, and black-box impossibilities between different types of qOWFs, qPKE, and EV-OWPuzz.
paper_structure: The paper develops by first presenting the negative result (separation of qPKE from qOWFs) using oracle constructions, followed by a positive construction showing qPKE can be built from quantum indistinguishability obfuscation and verifiable one-way puzzles.
why_interesting: While highly theoretical, the rigorous analysis of cryptographic assumptions in the quantum setting pushes the boundaries of what is computationally possible, which informs the theoretical limits of quantum information processing.
